In node2vec's Figure 3, the top visualization (label colors reflecting homophily) uses settings with q < 1, such as p = 1, q = 0.5, which give DFS-like, outward walks. These walks tend to embed nodes from the same network community close together, so the top panel illustrates homophily. Structural equivalence is shown in the bottom panel, which uses q > 1 (e.g., q = 2) and gives BFS-like, local walks that place structurally similar nodes, such as hubs or bridges, close together regardless of community. So no conditions make p = 1, q = 0.5 demonstrate structural equivalence; that setting favors homophily.
